title: Cells
lede: Every living thing is built from cells, and each cell runs like a small company: a head office, a power plant, a factory floor and a shipping dock.

sections.md:
## Cell theory
Three statements, worked out over 200 years, are the foundation of biology:

1. **All living things are made of one or more cells.**
2. **The cell is the basic unit of life.**
3. **All cells come from existing cells.**

Robert Hooke named cells in 1665 after looking at cork through an early microscope; the tiny boxes reminded him of monks' rooms (*cells*). It took until the 1850s for scientists to establish the third point: cells don't appear from nothing, they divide.

Your body has roughly **30 trillion** human cells, of about 200 types: muscle, nerve, blood, bone, skin.

## Two kinds of cells
| | **Prokaryotic** | **Eukaryotic** |
|---|---|---|
| Nucleus? | **No**: DNA floats in the cell | **Yes**: DNA enclosed in a nucleus |
| Organelles with membranes? | No | Yes |
| Size | small (about 1–10 µm) | larger (about 10–100 µm) |
| Examples | bacteria, archaea | animals, plants, fungi, protists |

*Pro* = before, *karyon* = kernel (nucleus): "before the nucleus." *Eu* = true. Prokaryotes came first; they were the only life on Earth for well over a billion years.

## Inside a eukaryotic cell: the company
| Organelle | Job | In the company |
|---|---|---|
| **Nucleus** | holds DNA, controls the cell | head office with the master plans |
| **Ribosomes** | build proteins | the factory floor |
| **Endoplasmic reticulum (ER)** | rough ER helps make proteins; smooth ER makes fats | assembly lines |
| **Golgi apparatus** | modifies, packages and ships proteins | the shipping dock |
| **Mitochondria** | turn food into usable energy (ATP) | the power plant |
| **Lysosomes** | break down waste and worn-out parts | recycling crew |
| **Cell membrane** | controls what goes in and out | the gate and security |
| **Cytoplasm** | gel filling the cell | the yard where everything happens |

## Plant cells add three things
- **Cell wall**: a rigid layer of cellulose outside the membrane. It's why plants stand up without bones.
- **Chloroplasts**: capture sunlight for **photosynthesis**. They contain the green pigment chlorophyll.
- **Large central vacuole**: a big water tank that keeps the cell firm. A wilting plant is one whose vacuoles are losing water.

Plant cells **also have mitochondria**. A common mistake is thinking chloroplasts replace them. Chloroplasts make sugar; mitochondria burn it.

sections.q: A cell has a nucleus, mitochondria, a cell wall and chloroplasts. It's most likely…
sections.why: Cell wall + chloroplasts = **plant**. A nucleus rules out bacteria. Viruses aren't cells at all.

sections.md:
## The membrane: a smart gate
The cell membrane is **selectively permeable**: some things pass freely, others need help.

- **Diffusion**: particles spread from where they're crowded to where they're sparse, with no energy needed. Oxygen enters your cells this way.
- **Osmosis**: diffusion of **water** across a membrane. Water moves toward the side with **more dissolved stuff** (higher solute concentration).
- **Active transport**: the cell spends energy to pump things **against** the gradient, like pushing a truck uphill.

Osmosis in action: put a red blood cell in salty water and water rushes **out**, so the cell shrivels. In pure water, water rushes **in** and the cell can burst. That's why IV fluids are matched to the salt level of blood.

## Why cells are so small
A cell feeds and breathes through its **surface**, but its needs grow with its **volume**. As anything gets bigger, volume grows faster than surface area:

| Cube side | Surface area | Volume | Surface : volume |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6 | 1 | **6 : 1** |
| 2 | 24 | 8 | **3 : 1** |
| 3 | 54 | 27 | **2 : 1** |

Triple the size and each unit of volume gets only one-third the surface to supply it. Past a certain size, a cell can't move materials in and out fast enough, so it divides. Big organisms are made of **many small cells**, not a few giant ones.

sections.label: Go deeper: mitochondria were once bacteria
sections.md: Mitochondria have their **own DNA**, their own ribosomes, and divide on their own, like bacteria. The leading explanation, **endosymbiotic theory**, is that over a billion years ago a larger cell swallowed a bacterium that survived inside it, and the two became partners. Chloroplasts likely began the same way, from photosynthetic bacteria. Your mitochondrial DNA comes almost entirely from your mother.

sections.label: Common traps
sections.md:
- **Viruses aren't cells.** They can't make energy or reproduce on their own; they hijack cells.
- **Plant cells have mitochondria too.**
- **Osmosis direction:** water moves **toward** the saltier side, not away from it.

practice.q: Which is part of cell theory?
options: All cells come from existing cells
Cells can form from non-living matter

practice.q: The main difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells is…
Which organelle releases energy from food?
practice.why: Mitochondria make ATP: the power plant.

practice.q: Which structure do plant cells have that animal cells don't?
A red blood cell placed in very salty water will…
practice.why: Water moves toward the saltier side: out of the cell.

practice.q: Moving a substance **against** its concentration gradient requires…
The Golgi apparatus is best compared to…
A cube-shaped cell has sides of 4 units. What is its surface-area-to-volume ratio? (Answer as a single number: SA ÷ V)
practice.why: SA = 6 × 4² = 96. V = 4³ = 64. 96 ÷ 64 = **1.5**. Compare 6 for a cube of side 1: bigger cells get much less surface per unit of volume.

practice.q: Mitochondria have their own DNA and divide on their own. This is key evidence for…
practice.why: They likely descend from bacteria that began living inside larger cells.

practice.q: A muscle cell has far more mitochondria than a skin cell. The best explanation:
options: Muscle cells need much more energy
practice.why: Cells build what their job demands. Endurance training even increases the number of mitochondria in muscle cells.
practice.hint: What do mitochondria make, and who needs a lot of it?

practice.q: Why can't a single cell grow to the size of a basketball?
options: It would run out of DNA
Its surface couldn't supply its huge volume fast enough
practice.why: Volume grows faster than surface area. The membrane is the only door, and a giant cell would starve in its center.
